item.text: {"chapter_id":"8B","shard_id":"8B-S05","reviewed_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E002","BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0032-E004","BATCH-0032-E005","BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0032-E007","BATCH-0032-E008","BATCH-0032-E009","BATCH-0032-E010","BATCH-0037-E003","BATCH-0037-E004","BATCH-0038-E001","BATCH-0038-E004","BATCH-0038-E006","BATCH-0038-E007","BATCH-0039-E001","BATCH-0039-E002","BATCH-0040-E005","BATCH-0040-E008","BATCH-0041-E001","BATCH-0041-E002","BATCH-0041-E003","BATCH-0041-E004","BATCH-0041-E005","BATCH-0041-E007","BATCH-0041-E008","BATCH-0042-E003","BATCH-0042-E006","BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0042-E009","BATCH-0042-E011","BATCH-0043-E001","BATCH-0043-E003","BATCH-0043-E005","BATCH-0043-E006","BATCH-0043-E007","BATCH-0043-E008","BATCH-0044-E005","BATCH-0044-E008","BATCH-0044-E009","BATCH-0044-E010","BATCH-0045-E008","BATCH-0045-E009","BATCH-0045-E011","BATCH-0045-E012","BATCH-0045-E013","BATCH-0046-E001","BATCH-0046-E002","BATCH-0046-E004","BATCH-0046-E006","BATCH-0046-E008","BATCH-0047-E001","BATCH-0047-E006","BATCH-0047-E007","BATCH-0047-E008","BATCH-0047-E009","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0047-E011","BATCH-0047-E012","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0048-E004","BATCH-0048-E005","BATCH-0048-E006","BATCH-0048-E009","BATCH-0048-E010","BATCH-0048-E012","BATCH-0048-E014","BATCH-0048-E015","BATCH-0049-E001","BATCH-0049-E005","BATCH-0049-E006","BATCH-0049-E010","BATCH-0049-E011"],"answers":[{"question_id":"8B.1","answer":"The shard documents a broad, repeatedly stated program: “Primero los pobres,” expanded social programs, state-led development, major infrastructure, energy sovereignty, public-security transformation, military-centered state capacity, environmental and multilateral commitments, and poverty reduction. Formal instruments included the 2022–2024 National Public Security Program and 2023 UN statements. However, some program evidence is bibliographic or retrospective, and official rhetoric does not itself establish operational clarity or consistency; electoral reform, militarization, energy policy, and environmental commitments reveal significant tensions.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0037-E003","BATCH-0038-E001","BATCH-0040-E005","BATCH-0044-E010","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0045-E008","BATCH-0045-E012","BATCH-0045-E013","BATCH-0046-E004","BATCH-0048-E014","BATCH-0048-E015"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0037-E004","BATCH-0038-E006","BATCH-0038-E007","BATCH-0042-E006","BATCH-0042-E009","BATCH-0046-E001","BATCH-0047-E006","BATCH-0047-E009","BATCH-0048-E004","BATCH-0049-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Several supplied records summarize books or speeches without substantive implementation evidence.","The shard does not establish which older proposals remained operative throughout 2023 or whether all stated goals formed one coherent frozen portfolio."]},{"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"The ruler’s government translated important priorities into formal machinery: mandatory national security objectives, strategies, actions, monitoring, oversight, and budget-funded implementation; expanded pensions and priority-program budgets; health-system restructuring; anti-inflation measures; a biosafety committee; military control of major functions; and proposed electoral and energy reforms. Execution machinery was often contested or incomplete, with judicial invalidation, missing environmental authorization, weak procurement controls, insufficient health investment, and opaque or incomplete project transfers.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0039-E002","BATCH-0041-E002","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0045-E008","BATCH-0045-E009","BATCH-0049-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0038-E004","BATCH-0042-E006","BATCH-0043-E006","BATCH-0043-E007","BATCH-0047-E012","BATCH-0047-E006","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0048-E004","BATCH-0048-E009","BATCH-0048-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal design and appropriations do not prove completed implementation.","Several adverse claims are external assessments, predictions, or allegations rather than final judicial or audit findings."]},{"question_id":"8B.3","answer":"There is evidence of substantial mobilization through pensions, social programs, infrastructure, military spending, the National Guard, and state-owned enterprises. The pension program expanded to 10.8 million beneficiaries with sharply higher spending; the 2023 social-program budget rose nominally; military allocations and responsibilities expanded. Countervailing records show budget displacement from health and other programs, procurement corruption risks, incomplete Tren Maya financial documentation, weak cybersecurity, and military expansion into tasks for which analysts considered the armed forces poorly prepared.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0041-E002","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0047-E001","BATCH-0049-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0040-E008","BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0045-E011","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0048-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Resource mobilization is better documented than whether mobilized resources achieved the ruler’s full portfolio.","Some evidence concerns 2022 or planned 2023 allocations rather than final 2023 execution."]},{"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"The shard shows appointment and replacement authority: Victoria Rodríguez was nominated and confirmed as Banco de México governor; Raquel Buenrostro replaced Economy Ministry personnel during active trade disputes; Ignacio Ovalle was removed from Segalmex but reassigned elsewhere; Javier May was appointed to lead Fonatur. These choices show active personnel management, but evidence is mixed on capability fit and results: some appointees had substantial technical experience, while other sources describe military personnel being assigned broad civilian functions despite limited preparation.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0039-E001","BATCH-0044-E005","BATCH-0046-E006","BATCH-0046-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0048-E012","BATCH-0047-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard rarely measures whether personnel choices improved execution.","The Banco de México record does not establish presidential motive, independence, or subsequent performance."]},{"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"Coordination and reach were demonstrated by national social-program coverage, federal ministry monitoring arrangements, territorial National Guard deployment, and extensive federal project administration. Yet implementation coordination was repeatedly impaired: health-system transition was associated with inadequate interinstitutional coordination; Sembrando Vida had supply, distribution, payment, planning, and monitoring bottlenecks; electoral reforms threatened territorial and professional capacity; Tren Maya transfer documentation remained incomplete; and military-led systems often lacked effective civilian oversight.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0048-E009","BATCH-0049-E001","BATCH-0049-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0041-E002","BATCH-0043-E006","BATCH-0043-E007","BATCH-0044-E008","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0048-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard provides limited systematic evidence on milestone completion across ministries and regions.","Some projected electoral harms were not verified as actual outcomes."]},{"question_id":"8B.6","answer":"Many formal decisions became observable practice: pensions and social programs operated at scale; Sembrando Vida and Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro delivered benefits and training; the National Security Program assigned mandatory implementation; infrastructure projects were built; and APECIC established operational price, import, monitoring, and sanction mechanisms. Delivery was mixed: AIFA remained heavily subsidy-dependent and below passenger targets; health access deteriorated after institutional transition; Tren Maya faced route changes, cost escalation, environmental/legal disputes, and audit irregularities; and some programs lacked controls, indicators, or adequate implementation capacity.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0041-E007","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0045-E008","BATCH-0045-E009","BATCH-0048-E009","BATCH-0049-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0041-E003","BATCH-0041-E004","BATCH-0042-E003","BATCH-0043-E005","BATCH-0044-E008","BATCH-0047-E006","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0048-E004","BATCH-0048-E005","BATCH-0048-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Some records describe planned or formal mechanisms without reporting their effectiveness.","The shard does not provide complete 2023 output data for every major program."]},{"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"Results were mixed relative to stated goals. Poverty and several social deprivations declined, pension coverage and older-person outcomes improved, and social transfers appear to have reduced aggregate poverty in a CONEVAL counterfactual. However, extreme poverty in absolute numbers increased, health-access deprivation rose sharply, Indigenous and disability gaps persisted or worsened, AIFA missed targets and required subsidies, health investment lagged, and security/militarization outcomes remained contested. Attribution is partial because outcomes also reflect pandemic recovery, demographic change, external shocks, and subnational action.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E002","BATCH-0032-E004","BATCH-0032-E005","BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0032-E009","BATCH-0042-E003","BATCH-0043-E005","BATCH-0046-E004","BATCH-0048-E009","BATCH-0048-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0032-E007","BATCH-0032-E008","BATCH-0032-E010","BATCH-0041-E004","BATCH-0047-E001","BATCH-0047-E009","BATCH-0048-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most outcome comparisons end in 2022 or use early-2023 reporting.","The shard does not supply a complete causal decomposition of ruler action, inherited conditions, shocks, and subordinate implementation."]},{"question_id":"8B.8","answer":"There is evidence of some adaptation: route changes and personnel replacement occurred in major projects and agencies; Sembrando Vida used local coordination to postpone planting and maintain unsuitable plants; the National Security Program required monitoring; and government institutional transitions continued in health. However, evaluations repeatedly identified unresolved weaknesses, including poor indicators, procurement and budget problems, cybersecurity deficiencies, health-investment under-execution, and accountability failures. The shard provides little proof that audits or failures consistently produced effective corrective action.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0044-E005","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0048-E009","BATCH-0049-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0045-E011","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0048-E004","BATCH-0048-E010","BATCH-0049-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence does not establish whether replacements or adaptations improved final outcomes.","Several cited evaluations predate 2023 and do not document subsequent response."]},{"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"The ruler and government responded to crises and resistance through institutional restructuring, military deployment, judicial and legislative contestation, diplomatic proposals, social transfers, anti-inflation measures, and public-security investigations. Some responses advanced control or program continuity, such as continuing Tren Maya after injunctions and expanding military responsibilities. Others exposed weak or contested crisis management: the Supreme Court invalidated National Guard militarization, health transition produced major access problems, electoral and transparency institutions were strained, alleged abuses lacked clearly independent investigation, and criticism of journalists and opponents generated reported threats and accountability concerns.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0038-E004","BATCH-0044-E009","BATCH-0044-E010","BATCH-0045-E008","BATCH-0045-E012","BATCH-0047-E008","BATCH-0049-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0041-E008","BATCH-0043-E001","BATCH-0047-E007","BATCH-0047-E011","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0048-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Many crisis-response records describe allegations, expert assessments, or projected consequences.","The shard does not establish the complete post-crisis institutional or legal outcomes in several cases."]},{"question_id":"8B.10","answer":"By the period’s end, the shard shows substantial conversion of selected priorities into durable programs, constitutional or statutory frameworks, budgets, infrastructure, military institutions, and state practice, especially pensions, social programs, National Guard expansion, and major projects. The end-state was nevertheless fragile and contradictory: health access worsened, poverty reductions coexisted with severe deprivation, AIFA and Tren Maya had financial or implementation weaknesses, procurement and transparency systems were impaired, military power expanded with limited civilian oversight, and several reforms faced judicial resistance. Durable achievement therefore cannot be inferred from formal architecture or survival alone.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E002","BATCH-0032-E004","BATCH-0032-E005","BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0041-E002","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0048-E014","BATCH-0049-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0032-E007","BATCH-0032-E008","BATCH-0040-E008","BATCH-0042-E003","BATCH-0043-E005","BATCH-0047-E009","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0048-E004","BATCH-0048-E012","BATCH-0049-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Several end-state assessments are retrospective or based on conditions before the end of 2023.","The shard lacks complete evidence on long-term durability, reversibility, final 2023 outcomes, and causal attribution across the full program portfolio."]}],"cross_shard_cautions":["All findings are confined to supplied shard records and cited only by their supplied evidence IDs.","The evidence is concentrated in social policy, health, infrastructure, security, militarization, transparency, and selected foreign-policy materials; it does not comprehensively cover every possible program component.","No score or confidence judgment is made here."]}
